title: Test Worker death after exec before process registration
description: The launch-gap experiment closes the pre-exec phantom. It does not establish discovery or cleanup when the OS child starts and Worker death occurs before the child registers. Construct this later boundary with a child-side pre-registration barrier, then test fenced replacement, stale registration rejection, surviving-process discovery, and cleanup/credential revocation.
acceptance_criteria: A real child survives Worker SIGKILL while blocked before registration; retry behavior is reproduced under control and fenced recovery; stale registration/effects fail closed; process discovery and cleanup observations are preserved; destination/credential assumptions are explicit.

title: Experiment: external effect succeeds before Activity completion is lost
description: Build the next failure-boundary experiment: an external effect succeeds, the Worker dies before Temporal records Activity completion, and retry observes ambiguity. Compare an idempotent endpoint, a non-idempotent endpoint, a transactional database mutation, Git/worktree mutation, message publication, and artifact creation without claiming exactly-once behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Each destination has a stated invariant, exact post-effect/pre-completion barrier, unsafe control, destination-specific protected mechanism, repeated race-enabled live trials, raw evidence, responsibility split, and falsifier; docs/guarantees.md and findings are updated.

title: Reconcile launch decisions without registered child processes
description: The application store records a launch decision before the OS child is successfully started and registered. If launch fails or the Worker dies in that window, reattachment can wait forever on a phantom executor. Add a deterministic experiment before changing the protocol.
acceptance_criteria: A failing reproduction kills/fails between durable launch decision and process registration; the evidence preserves the phantom-owner failure; the minimal recovery protocol distinguishes pending launch from live registered executor and either safely retries launch or replaces with fencing.
notes:
Independent milestone review confirmed the current reattach protocol can wait on a durable launch decision whose child never registered. This remains deliberately unfixed until its failure is captured at an exact post-decision/pre-launch or pre-registration barrier; do not add a PID-missing heuristic.
Completed exact post-launch-decision/pre-process-launch reproduction. Preserved v1/v2 development evidence and final v3 control/recovery evidence. The control records an attempt-2 attachment to a PID-less launch_pending executor; indefinite waiting is an implementation inference, while server-visible retry heartbeat remains unresolved in temporal_projects-79z. The minimal protocol adds explicit launch_pending/running/completed lifecycle, fenced conditional replacement only for pending launches, monotonic Temporal-attempt checks, registration-gated mutation, and exact barrier identity validation. Final v3 recovery has one accepted generation-2 effect/outcome and matching Workflow/application results. Validation: go test -race -timeout 4m ./..., 85.1% coverage, go vet, staticcheck, go mod verify, govulncheck, replay tests, evidence JSON validation, and independent code/security reviews with no CRITICAL or HIGH findings.

title: Experiment: CompleteActivityByID stale-attempt semantics
description: Construct a live reproduction for source-observed CompleteActivityByID behavior after an Activity retry. Separate stale original task-token completion, completion by logical Activity ID, and application-level stale-writer fencing.
acceptance_criteria: A real Temporal service test captures the old attempt, forces retry, attempts both completion paths, records exact service responses/history, and documents observed semantics without extrapolating beyond the tested Server/SDK versions.

title: Milestone 1: worker death with surviving agent
description:
## Why
Establish the Agent Durability Lab and produce executable evidence for a Temporal Activity whose Worker dies while an independently running agent process survives.

## Scope
Create operating guidance and minimum research documentation; implement deterministic unsafe, stable-identity/reattachment, and fenced-ownership variants; preserve event evidence; integrate with the Temporal Go SDK; and test the precise failure boundaries without sleep-based coordination.
design: Single-machine laboratory. Use a durable application work store for logical sessions/generations and an append-only JSONL event ledger. Use explicit named barriers for failure injection. Keep Temporal workflow orchestration thin and deterministic. Run Temporal SDK testsuite for Workflow/Activity contract plus a subprocess E2E harness for launcher death; document where a live Temporal service remains required for true Worker-process death validation.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md contain concise lab rules; guarantees and methodology docs distinguish Temporal, application, and external-system responsibility; tests first demonstrate duplicate writers in unsafe mode, reattachment by stable session identity, and stale-completion rejection by fencing; a real child process can outlive its launcher; a Temporal workflow/activity integration test proves retry after lost Activity completion; deterministic repeated trials pass under go test -race ./... with at least 80% package coverage; control evidence and findings are preserved.
notes: Completed with final v3 evidence under Go 1.25.12. Final verification: go test -race -timeout 4m ./... (two live trials per arm), make coverage 84.7%, go vet, staticcheck, go mod verify, and govulncheck clean. Independent code/simplification/security reviews completed; HIGH findings were fixed and re-verified. Original and v2 evidence remain preserved; docs point to v3.
close_reason: Milestone acceptance satisfied: real Worker death/surviving child experiment, unsafe/reattach/fenced evidence, replay/nondeterminism checks, repeated race trials, 84.7% core coverage, findings/guarantees, and reviewed security remediations are complete.

title: Observe heartbeat visibility during phantom reattachment
description: A stronger launch-gap control attempted to wait until DescribeWorkflowExecution exposed heartbeat details for Activity attempt 2 before cancellation. One of two live trials reached the overall deadline without that exact observation. Build a focused reproduction that distinguishes SDK heartbeat calls, server-persisted heartbeat details, Activity attempt compaction, and Describe visibility without upgrading inference to observation.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the failing/variable history and Describe snapshots; use an exact synchronization protocol; state which heartbeat call and attempt the server durably observed; document what can and cannot be used as an operator liveness signal.

title: Harden failure-injection evidence authenticity
description: The loopback barrier trusts all same-host processes. A local process can forge the first arrival and cause the controller to inject a fault at a false boundary. Add identity binding only when experiments move beyond a trusted single-user lab.
acceptance_criteria: The controller pre-registers expected session/generation/actor/barrier identities, requests are authenticated with per-run credentials, forged/replayed arrivals fail closed, and raw credentials never enter portable evidence.

title: Experiment: agent session compatibility across Worker Versioning deployments
description: Run long-lived external sessions across pinned and auto-upgrade Worker deployments; distinguish Workflow replay compatibility, Activity implementation compatibility, and the detached agent protocol/build contract.
acceptance_criteria: Replay-safe and deliberately incompatible changes are tested on a real service; retry/reattachment across versions records Worker deployment and agent-build identity; incompatible attachment fails closed.

title: Experiment: partial Workflow Stream output and retry reconstruction
description: Measure consumer-observed prefixes, publisher identity, duplicate output, buffered-event loss, ordering, and resumption when a Worker dies during Workflow Stream publication.
acceptance_criteria: Current Public Preview API is used; exact stream boundaries and durable consumer observations are preserved; retries test publisher identity and duplicate handling; conclusions state what lives in history versus external state.

title: Experiment: large artifact write/reference/acknowledgement windows
description: Test large output and code-patch artifacts across object write, reference creation, reference persistence, Activity completion, and consumer acknowledgement failures, including Temporal External Storage where applicable.
acceptance_criteria: Each boundary has an orphan/loss/duplication oracle, content hashes and durable references are recorded, cleanup/reconciliation is explicit, and payload size is kept out of Workflow history where intended.

title: Compare Workflow orchestration with Standalone Activity durability
description: Implement matched experiments using a Workflow plus Activity and a current Standalone Activity to answer when durable execution is sufficient versus when a durable orchestration state machine adds necessary state/order.
acceptance_criteria: The same effect/failure invariant runs through both primitives on supported current versions; operational state, replay value, retry semantics, and failure behavior are measured and documented.

title: Experiment: precise cancellation across Worker death and ownership change
description: Test cancellation for healthy Worker, killed Worker with surviving child, temporarily unreachable child, owner replacement, and cancellation/completion races. Cancellation must name session and generation and fail closed for stale executors.
acceptance_criteria: Each cancellation boundary uses deterministic coordination, proves the exact targeted process/generation, records delivery and acknowledgement separately, and documents what Temporal versus the application guarantees.
notes: Security review found current teardown checks /proc start identity then sends SIGKILL in a separate syscall and targets only the leader despite Setpgid. The cancellation experiment must evaluate pidfd-based exact identity plus process-group/cgroup descendant control; do not generalize current cleanup into a cancellation guarantee.

title: Experiment: observability of wedged agents versus legitimate waits
description: Define and test application signals that distinguish healthy Temporal retry, permanently failing retry, live-but-wedged child, dead Worker with healthy child, stale executor, ambiguous effect, and legitimate Workflow wait.
acceptance_criteria: A single-machine operator can classify each injected state from preserved Temporal and application signals without inspecting process internals; false-positive/false-negative observations and blind spots are documented.
